sentences.text: Misc. Appeal No. 4380 of 2023

Gopal Tailor
 Versus
 Sushil And Others
 Appearance:
Shri Neeraj Gour, learned counsel with Shri Romil Ma  counsel for the appellant.
Shri Sudarshan Pandit, learned counsel for responden  ORDER 1.
With the consent of learned counsel for parties the matter is finally heard.

2. This appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellant/claimant being aggrieved by the award dated 24.02.2023 passed in MACC No.371/2016 by the 27th Additional Member, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Indore whereby a total sum of Rs.1,72,524/-
has been awarded to him by way of compensation.
3. As per the appellant, on 19.04.2013 he along with his wife was going on a motorcycle from Ashta to Indore.

When they reached Pilwani culvert in Sonkatch respondent No.1, the owner and driver of the offending vehicle a motorcycle bearing registration No.MP-09-ND-6072 which was insured with respondent No.2, drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the same against his motorcycle as a result of which he fell down and suffered 2 MA-4380-2023 grievous injuries.
He was taken to the hospital for treatment where he remained under treatment for a considerable period of time.
4. The appellant thereafter filed an application under Section 166 of the Act, 1988 before the Claims Tribunal for award of a total sum of Rs.15,12,990/- to him by way of compensation.
The application was contested by respondent No.2 by filing its written statement to the same.
Upon evaluation of the evidence brought on record by the parties the Claims Tribunal has awarded compensation to the appellant as aforesaid.

sentences.text: 5. This appeal for enhancement of the amount of compensation has been preferred by the appellant on the ground that in the accident he had suffered permanent disability to the extent of 23%.
The same was proved by him by proving the Permanent Disability Certificate.
However, the Claims Tribunal has erred in assessing the permanent disability at 8% only.
It is further submitted that the amount awarded to the appellant for special diet, attendant and transportation is also very low.
It is hence submitted that the amount awarded to the appellant be enhanced appropriately.

6. Per contra learned counsel for respondent No.2 has submitted that just and fair amount of compensation has been awarded to the appellant in which no interference is warranted in view of which the appeal deserves to be dismissed.
7. I have considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and have perused the record.
8. In the accident the appellant had suffered fracture of tibia of left knee, fracture of clavicle bone in the right shoulder and fracture of metacarpal bone on the right hand.
Though operations were performed upon them but the bones in the body of the appellant are not straight.

There is 10%
deviation in his left leg and his walk is 15 degree slow.
In his right hand there is 20% deviation.
On the basis 3 MA-4380-2023 of the same Dr. Ashish Jain, who was examined before the Tribunal had proved the permanent disability certificate of the appellant.
Therein though he stated the permanent disability to be 23% but even for the entire body the same could not have been taken to be a mere 8%.

Looking to the injuries suffered by the appellant the same deserves to be taken at 17%.
9.

The amount which the appellant would be entitled for on account of his permanent disability would hence be Rs.6,000/- per month plus 10% for future prospects of rise in income multiplied by 12 for making it annually.
The multiplier of 11 applied by the Tribunal is correct.
The permanent disability is taken at 17%.
Thus under this head the appellant would be entitled for a sum of Rs.1,48,104/-.
The amount awarded for special diet, attendant and transportation is also low.
The same deserves to be awarded at Rs.10,000/- each.
10. The appellant is entitled for award of a total sum of Rs.2,70,392/- to him by way of compensation whereas the Claims Tribunal has erred in awarding him a sum of Rs.1,72,524/- only.

The appellant is hence held entitled for enhancement in the award of compensation0 by a sum of Rs.97,868/- which shall be paid to him along with the same rate of interest as awarded by the Claims Tribunal from the date of filing of the claim application till date of payment.
11. The appeal is accordingly partly allowed and disposed off.
(PRANAY VERMA) JUDGE ns
